A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, with M2M renamed Mirage. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's supplementary Appendices A–D; v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: Section V reports original experiments on three image-classification datasets, including attack comparisons, persistence evaluations and ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original experimental results and adds non-IID sensitivity results; Appendix C reports expanded attacker-count experiments.

M1.justification: The detector-based construction and mapping-enhancement components remain. Algorithm 1 changes the specified trigger update from lambda1-weighted detector loss plus lambda2-weighted enhancement loss to their unweighted sum. The PDFs do not establish whether this changed the executed experiments.

E1.justification: Both evaluate federated image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and GTSRB, including blended and pixel-trigger scenarios. The added heterogeneity and attacker-count sweeps vary configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Both compare against Vanilla, PGD, Neurotoxin, Chameleon and A3FL. Table I/Table 1 retains the same defense conditions: Multi-Krum, DeepSight, Foolsgold, RFLBAT, FLAME and BackdoorIndicator, plus no defense.

E3.justification: V2 adds a Dirichlet-alpha sweep over 0.5, 1, 5, 10 and 1000, and extends the one-to-five-attacker protocol to CIFAR-100 and GTSRB. The default client selection, training settings, metrics and poisoning window remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 adds sensitivity analysis for client-data heterogeneity, while Appendix C extends the existing attacker-count analysis beyond CIFAR-10. The architecture study, enhancement ablation, feature-distribution analysis and pixel-trigger investigation are retained.

E5.justification: Both report mean attacker ASR and attacker spread without specifying independent repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's additional individual-attacker results do not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table I/Table 1 is numerically unchanged. V2 adds non-IID results, including CIFAR-10 ASRs of 98.80–99.39% in Table 3, and additional attacker-count and individual-attacker results in Table 5. It also corrects the reported post-poisoning lifespan from over 1000 to over 900 rounds.

T1.justification: The detector-data definition and adversarial and enhancement formulations remain equivalent in v1 Equations 2–4 and v2 Equations 1–3. No substantive theoretical assumptions, proofs or derivations are added. Removing the generic FL overview and aggregation equation is an expository change.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly claims the first non-cooperative MBA strategy in its abstract and conclusion; v1's explicit priority claim concerned explaining multi-adversary interference. The central ID-mapping, effectiveness and persistence contributions remain, with quantitative performance summaries added to the abstract.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 revises the explanation of Indicator failures from checking the largest-ASR label to limited OOD mappings and differences between dynamic and static attacks. Section 6.2 newly states that one-shot attacks have low durability and side effects on the main task.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly documents freezing the detector's feature extractor, specifies a 5×5 top-left pixel patch, and adds dataset details and an algorithm walkthrough. Its abstract replaces the promise of future code release with an open-source statement and hyperlink; this establishes changed access information within the PDF.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including KDE, FedScale and HarmoFL, while removing BadCleaner, FLPurifier and some application references. Related-work discussion is condensed and DBA joins NBA as the closest work, while the substantive distinction from NBA remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations and discussion. It replaces the Preliminaries structure with a dedicated Attack Intuitions section, moves the threat model into Methodology, adds supplementary Appendices A–D and systematically renames M2M to Mirage.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figures 1–3, reformats the main comparison table, converts architecture and attacker-count charts into tables, and rearranges the six-panel t-SNE display into one row. It clarifies persistence-plot axes and poisoning timing, adds result tables and moves the pixel-trigger figure to the supplement.

improvement.justification: Clearer explanations and redesigned figures improve readability, while the heterogeneity sweep and expanded attacker-count results modestly strengthen empirical support. Added implementation and code-access information improve reproducibility documentation, and the lifespan correction removes an overstatement. These are useful incremental gains to a paper whose central benchmark evidence remains unchanged.
